name: Motivated Focus Transfer and Reveal
summary: Move the viewer's gaze from a known object or question to a specific hidden detail, then hold long enough for comprehension.

intent.viewerQuestion: What detail am I supposed to notice, and why does it matter?
intent.desiredPerceptualResult: One clear primary focus at each beat; the discovered detail feels caused by the setup rather than an unrelated visual flourish.
avoidWhen: Two independent facts require simultaneous reading.
A subject lacks a readable silhouette or useful contrast.
The reveal would interrupt necessary diagram continuity.

visibleCues: The first subject has the highest legibility and local contrast.
An occluder, framing move, focus change, or nearby annotation transfers attention.
The new detail becomes unambiguously readable before the next edit.
plausibleCauses: Selective lighting or material contrast, without implying physically impossible lights.
Depth-of-field change when text and detail remain legible.
unknowns: A viewer's actual gaze path cannot be proven from pixels alone.
Depth-of-field may be generated by lens blur, postprocessing, or a 2.5D mask.

beats.direction: Show the complete mechanism and maintain a quiet stable camera. Establish the relevant subject's shape and orientation.
Use a single motivated camera or occlusion movement toward the useful joint. Lower competing contrast only after the subject is established; preserve screen direction.
Settle all nonessential movement. Hold the revealed contact, add one concise pointer if needed, then demonstrate the causal action.

craftNotes: Avoid simultaneous camera, light, text and particle transitions; one change should own the viewer's attention.
Keep enough edge and texture detail to read the reveal at final output resolution, not only in a zoomed Storybook preview.
Use hierarchy, occlusion and relative motion before relying on blur or bloom.
recipe.fallback: Use a static camera and sequential localized highlights with a restrained annotation if 3D reframing or depth effects fail quality review.

parameters.name: transferStartFraction
parameters.visualImpact: Controls how long the audience can orient before attention moves.
failureSigns: Reveal begins before the object is understood.

parameters.name: settleHoldFraction
parameters.visualImpact: Reserves readable time after the focus transfer.
failureSigns: Cut arrives before the viewer can identify the detail.

parameters.name: secondaryContrastScale
parameters.visualImpact: Subordinates competing regions without erasing material definition.
failureSigns: Background vanishes into black or looks like an artificial vignette.

kumiki.adapterNotes: Compose existing camera/lighting controls with a deterministic three-beat attention timeline; do not invent an independent renderer clock.

acceptanceChecks: Mute narration: a reviewer can point to the intended focus on every beat at normal playback speed.
The revealed detail is fully visible for the final hold and is not clipped in 16:9 or 9:16 framing.
No flash, depth blur or competing title obscures the mechanical explanation.
